Despite improvements in the fields of surgery and radiation therapy, the prognosis remains poor for human patients diagnosed with this tumor type as most succumb to local tumor recurrence. Using the dog as a model for the human disease may help speed progress in developing new approaches to treatment of this cancer. Sinonasal carcinoma occurs commonly in dogs and is primarily treated with radiation therapy. Like humans, most dogs succumb to local tumor recurrence. With these clinical similarities, dogs could fill an unmet need for an effective model for human sinonasal carcinoma.
